cards.text: David is king over Israel, and a famine hits for three years in a row. Not one bad year. Not two. THREE. So David seeks the face of the LORD.

cards.question: David asks the LORD about the three-year famine. What does the LORD say it's because of?

answers.text: Blood Saul shed killing the Gibeonites
Idols the people set up in the land

cards.text: So David calls in the Gibeonites. Quick background, friend: they're not Israelites. They're what's left of the Amorites.

cards.question: The Israelites had taken an oath concerning the Gibeonites, and Saul kept it.

cards.text: In his zeal for Israel and Judah, Saul sought to kill them. Saul's gone now, but the problem just landed on David's desk.

cards.question: David asks the Gibeonites how he can make amends. What does he hope they'll do after?

answers.text: Bless the inheritance of the LORD

cards.question: The Gibeonites tell David they need no ___ or ___ from Saul or his house.

cards.text: They also tell David he shouldn't put anyone in Israel to death for them. 'Whatever you ask, I will do for you,' he replies, and friend, those are BIG words to say before you've heard the ask.

cards.question: The Gibeonites name the man who plotted to wipe them out of Israel. What do they ask David to hand over?

answers.text: Half of the land Saul held

cards.text: They want to hang the seven before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul.

cards.question: David turns down the Gibeonites' request for seven of Saul's descendants.

cards.text: But one of Saul's grandsons is spared: Mephibosheth, the son of Saul's son Jonathan.

cards.question: Why does David spare Mephibosheth son of Jonathan?

answers.text: Because of his oath with Jonathan
Because the Gibeonites left him out
Because Mephibosheth was still a child

cards.text: Careful now, friend, because there's ANOTHER Mephibosheth, a son of Saul himself. Two Mephibosheths in one story, like two guys named Mike on the same work team.

cards.question: David takes this other Mephibosheth and his brother Armoni. Who was their mother?

cards.text: Then David takes the sons of Saul's daughter Merab, the sons she bore to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

cards.question: Two sons from Rizpah plus ___ sons from Merab make the seven the Gibeonites asked for.

cards.text: David hands all seven over to the Gibeonites. They hang them on the hill before the LORD, and all seven fall together.

cards.question: The seven are put to death at the beginning of the ___ harvest.

cards.text: Now watch Rizpah, the mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth. She takes sackcloth and spreads it out for herself on a rock.

cards.question: Day and night on that rock, what does Rizpah keep away from the bodies?

answers.text: Birds by day and beasts by night
Thieves by day and soldiers by night
Strangers by day and robbers by night

cards.question: Rizpah keeps watch over the bodies from the beginning of the harvest until the rain from heaven pours down on them.

cards.text: Somebody tells David what Rizpah has done. So David goes and gets the bones of Saul and Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them after the Philistines struck Saul down at Gilboa.

cards.question: The Philistines had hung the bodies of Saul and Jonathan in the public square of ___.
David brings back the bones of Saul and Jonathan but leaves the bones of the seven who were hanged where they are.

cards.text: They bury the bones of Saul and Jonathan in Zela, in the land of Benjamin.

cards.question: In Zela, whose tomb are Saul and Jonathan buried in?
They do everything King David commanded. What happens after that?

answers.text: God answers their prayers for the land
The Gibeonites move away from Israel
Saul's family turns against King David

findings.problem: The opening card has five sentences: 'David is king over Israel, and a famine hits for three years in a row.' 'Not one bad year.' 'Not two.' 'THREE.' 'So David seeks the face of the LORD.' That is over the limit of three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

findings.problem: 'Saul's gone now' states that Saul is dead. That fact does not come from 2 Samuel 21:2, the only verse the card cites. Saul's death is told in 1 Samuel 31, and the passage mentions it only later, in 2 Samuel 21:12. The card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This card asks the baker to fill in the exact wording 'silver or gold' from 2 Samuel 21:4. No earlier card lets the baker reason it out, so it tests wording, not meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The right answers depend on order: silver is blank 1 and gold is blank 2. 'Gold or silver' means the same thing, so a baker who swaps them could fairly argue they are right and still be marked as missed.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The question says 'The Gibeonites name the man who plotted to wipe them out of Israel.' In 2 Samuel 21:5 they never name him. They say only 'the man who consumed us and plotted against us.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This story card is one plain sentence with no context and none of Papa Dorin's voice: 'They want to hang the seven before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul.'

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: 'Somebody tells David what Rizpah has done. So David goes...' The word 'So' makes Rizpah's actions the reason David acts. The text says only 'When David was told... he went' (2 Samuel 21:11-12) and does not say why.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This story card packs in more than two beats: David is told about Rizpah, David goes and gets the bones, the men of Jabesh-gilead had stolen them, and the Philistines struck Saul down at Gilboa.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Most story cards in this stop are bare retellings with no trace of Papa Dorin. Cards 5, 7 and 15 have no voice at all ('They bury the bones of Saul and Jonathan in Zela, in the land of Benjamin.'). The only personality in the whole stop is the line about two guys named Mike on card 3.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
